chunks: I wrote to the man (peace be upon him) that those before us from your followers have differed regarding tawhid — some of them say 'a body' and some of them say 'a form'.

So he (peace be upon him) wrote in his own handwriting: Glorified is the One Who cannot be limited, nor can He be described. There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing — or he said: the All-Seeing.

key_terms.التوحيد: Tawhid — Divine Unity, here specifically the question of God's nature and transcendence
key_terms.جسم: Jism — body, corporeal substance; the heretical view that God has a physical body
key_terms.صورة: Sura — form, shape; another anthropomorphic description rejected by the Imam
key_terms.لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ: There is nothing like unto Him — direct Quranic quotation (42:11)
key_terms.يُحَدُّ: Yuhaddu — to be limited, bounded, circumscribed; God cannot be delimited
key_terms.يُوصَفُ: Yusaf — to be described with attributes; God transcends human description

ai.seo_question: What did the Imam say about God having a body or form in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith records a written response from Imam Ali al-Hadi (peace be upon him) to a question about a theological dispute among his followers regarding the nature of God. Some claimed God has a 'body' (jism) while others claimed He has a 'form' (sura). The Imam responded in his own handwriting, quoting and affirming the Quranic principle that God is utterly transcendent, beyond all limitation and description, citing the divine attributes of hearing and knowledge (or sight) from Surah al-Shura 42:11. This response stands as a definitive Imami rejection of anthropomorphism (tashbih) and affirms God's absolute incomparability (tanzih).
